exercise.name: Curtsy Lunge
library_steps: Stand tall, holding a dumbbell at each side.
Step one foot behind and across the other, like a curtsy.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, chest up.
Drive off your front heel to return, then switch legs.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing with dumbbells at the sides, the right foot steps back and across behind the left; both knees bend until the back knee is just above the floor, chest up, most weight on the front (left) leg.

setup.target: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell hanging at each side, palms in.
Most of the weight stays on the front leg; the back leg is for balance.
setup.tolerance: front foot flat, back foot on the ball

movement.end: about 85-90 deg, knee over the mid-foot, not caving in

movement.measure: knee flexion; height of the knee joint above the floor
movement.end: about 75-80 deg, knee joint ~0.20 m above the floor (kneecap a hand-width off it)

movement.measure: right ankle relative to left ankle
movement.end: about 0.8 m behind and crossed ~0.23 m toward the left (x +0.10), heel up
movement.tolerance: crossed past the midline, behind the front foot

movement.start: hanging at the sides holding dumbbells

muscles.role: Library primary. Transverse (crossing) lunge gave the highest gluteal EMG of the lunges in Distefano's data quoted by S1 (49% MVIC max, 48% med).
Extends the front knee; vasti were the most active muscles in lunges and step-ups in S4.
Keeps the front knee and pelvis from caving in; library secondary.
Co-contract at the hip and knee (biceps femoris lower than quads/glutes in lunges).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Front knee drops inside the big toe at the bottom.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Loads the knee badly and takes the glute out of the move.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Torso shifts back over the rear foot.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The front glute does less of the work.

sources.citation: Boren K, Conrey C, Le Coguic J, et al. 2011. Electromyographic analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises. Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223.
sources.what_it_gave: Table 1 (summary of Distefano): forward lunge 44/42, sideways 41/39, transverse lunge 49/48 % MVIC glut max/med.

sources.citation: The Prehab Guys. Curtsey lunge (exercise library).
sources.what_it_gave: Step back and across like a curtsy; keep most weight on the front leg; do not let the front knee cave in or bow out.
